question: Does adding one pre-match-frozen CRS opportunity satellite to two pre-existing A1/A2 direction anchors, with pair-plus-triple coverage, improve cost-matched portfolio outcomes without forcing weak anchors or hiding true ticket expansion?
hypothesis: A separately gated CRS satellite can add payout convexity while the anchor-anchor pair preserves some portfolio survival when the exact score misses.
comparison_arms: B: standalone CRS satellite plus anchor_1 x anchor_2
C: pure satellite x anchor_1 x anchor_2 triple
mandatory_freeze_fields: primitive bet count and total cost

reject_or_keep_shadow_if: Any benefit disappears after exact primitive-bet cost matching.
Performance is dominated by one or two rare CRS hits with unstable payout concentration.
The template causes B/C matches to be promoted merely to fill anchor slots.
Score selections are chosen or changed after observing the result.
Mixed-pool compatibility is assumed rather than observed.
Nominal 3x4 labels understate true cost when legs contain multiple selections.
ROI improvement comes with materially worse drawdown without a preregistered acceptable tradeoff.
The effect is confined to one league or short time window and fails walk-forward stability.
